title: How To Get Your Students To Do Their Homework https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2014/04/12/how-to-get-your-students-to-do-their-homework/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin addresses the perennial challenge of homework completion by outlining four guidelines for how it should be structured and checked. He argues homework must be pure practice of material students have already mastered independently in class, since assigning material they don't yet understand saps motivation. He recommends nightly rather than weekly assignments to reinforce same-day learning and reduce procrastination or copying, and he prescribes a personal, in-person homework check each morning as the most powerful accountability tool. The piece ties homework completion back to the broader relationship between teacher and student, arguing that respect and trust extend the teacher's influence into the home.
points: Homework should only cover material students have already proven they can do independently during the school day—never new or unclear content.
Teachers who hover and over-help during independent practice create a culture of dependence that shows up as failed homework.
Nightly homework reinforces same-day learning better than weekly packets, and reduces procrastination and copying.
Checking homework personally and publicly each morning, student by student, is described as the single most important homework tool.
A student's motivation to complete homework is largely a function of the trust and respect built through the classroom relationship.
quotes: Homework can be particularly frustrating because it takes place outside of your presence.
It isn’t fair to them to struggle through work they don’t fully comprehend. Even one time will sap their motivation for completing future assignments.
As a result, their students become so accustomed to receiving immediate, extensive, and personal help that when it’s time to truly do it on their own, which is usually at home, they’re lost.
I recommend having your students set it out neatly on their desk as part of your morning routine.
This underscores the importance of building rapport and mutual likability with your students, while at the same time faithfully doing exactly what you say you will.
